Recognize safety information. This is the safety-alert symbol . When you see this symbol on the unit and in instructions or manuals, be alert to the potential for personal injury. Understand these signal words; DANGER, WARNING, and CAUTION. These words are used with the safety-alert symbol. DANGER identifies the most serious hazards which will result in severe personal injury or death. WARNING signifies hazards which could result in personal injury or death. CAUTION is used to identify unsafe practices which may result in minor personal injury or product and property damage. GENERAL DC Power System Installation Guidelines Requirements and Restrictions for Residential Applications Overview The DC Power System is designed and approved exclusively for single dwelling residential applications. To ensure safe operation, system reliability, and warranty protection, strict adherence to the following installation requirements is mandatory. Permitted Installation Locations • Concrete pad at ground level • Composite pad at ground level Installation must occur only on a ground-level concrete or composite pad. This ensures system stability, proper grounding, and compliance with manufacturer safety protocols. Prohibited Installation Locations • Rooftops • Racks • Frames • Any structure other than a ground-level concrete or composite pad • Flood zones The DC Power System must not be installed on rooftops, racks, frames, or any elevated or alternative structures. Installation in flood zones or areas lacking adequate drainage is strictly prohibited. Such practices may result in system malfunction, increased safety hazards, and/or voided warranty. Application Restrictions • Single dwelling residential properties only • Multi-dwelling residences, commercial, or industrial properties are not permitted This system is intended solely for single dwelling residential use. Installation in any other property type is not allowed and may void system certification and warranty. Altitude Limitation Maximum installation altitude: 6,500 ft. (2,000 meters) above sea level. Do not install the DC Power System above the specified altitude limit, as performance and safety may be compromised beyond this threshold. Drainage Requirement Installation should be carried out only in areas with adequate drainage to prevent water accumulation and potential damage to the system. Consequences of Non-Compliance Failure to comply with the above requirements may result in: • System malfunction • Voided warranty • Safety hazards For optimal performance and safety, follow all installation guidelines precisely. Pre-Installation Checklist for DC Power System Checklist for Installing or Servicing the DC Power System 1. Turn Off Power: Before beginning any installation or service work, always turn off power to the Outdoor Unit using the outdoor unit disconnect switch. 2. Consult Site Plan: Review the site plan to confirm the designated installation location of the DC Power System. 3. Verify Proper Location: Ensure the unit is installed at least 3 feet away from windows, doors, and other units according to NFPA 855 and IRC requirements. 4. Inspect Components: Before installation, carefully inspect all components of the DC Power System for any signs of damage or corrosion, including the battery, cable harnesses, control boards, and electrical panels. 5. Check Shipping Packing List: Verify that all components listed on the shipping packing list are present and accounted for. 6. Ensure Weather-Proofing: Confirm that the DC Power System control board enclosures are weather-proof to prevent exposure and damage. 7. Document and Report Issues: If any damage or missing components are discovered, document the findings and report them to the Supplier. Do not install any component that appears damaged. 8. Verify Grounding: Check that the DC Power System is properly grounded according to NFPA 855.15.4.1. Refer to “Connecting Quick Connect Cables to the Battery” section of the installation instructions for proper ground connection procedures. Following this checklist will help ensure a safe, compliant, and successful installation or servicing of your DC Power System. DC Power System Shipping Contents The following items will be included in the DC Power System shipment: • Daughter Board • Necessary harness • Anchor straps • Labels Please verify that all listed components are present upon receipt. If any items are missing, contact your supplier or technical support team for assistance. General Clearance Requirements Refer to Fig. 2. When installing the unit, it is essential to allow adequate space for airflow, wiring, refrigerant piping, and service access. To ensure safe and efficient operation, maintain the following clearances: • Allow at least 24 inches (610 mm) of clearance at the Battery access panel. • Maintain a minimum of 96 inches (2.4 m) of clearance above the unit. • Provide 6 inches (152 mm) of clearance on one side of the unit and 12 inches (305 mm) on all remaining sides for proper airflow. • Keep a distance of 36 inches (914 mm) between units and between the unit and any doors or windows. Location and Environmental Considerations Position the unit so that water, snow, or ice from the roof or eaves cannot fall directly onto it. This helps prevent potential damage and ensures reliable operation. Additionally, the installation site should allow water to drain away from the unit. Code Compliance and Safety Distances According to NFPA 855 and the International Residential Code (IRC), units should be installed at least 3 feet away from doors, windows, and other units. Separation distances from walls and other units should follow the allowances determined by UL9540A testing. The suggested separation distances provided above are recommended pending the results of UL9540A testing and internal safety evaluations. Always consult the latest code requirements and manufacturer guidelines when planning installation. Avoid direct sunlight, rain and/or snow exposure to the Battery during installation. Do not install the DC Power System outside the recommended temperature and humidity range. CABATTRY: Installation Instructions Start-Up Commissioning Steps: 1. Perform the following before starting the commissioning steps. – Verify correct placement of DC Power System – Verify correct wiring – Verify correct (physical) Cellular Antenna placement – Verify correct signage 2. Close electrical disconnects to energize system. 3. Power On Sequence – Turn AC service disconnect ON – Wait 1 minute for the DC Power System to power ON and allow it to run/complete Power On Self Test 4. Connect Service Tech App (STA) to the DC Power System. – Utilizing the STA, perform cloud telemetry/commands test report results Note: Safely pause cloud Control commands if you need to re-commission. – Follow the steps displayed on STA for commissioning. – STA will display results screen of commissioning – STA will save/email commissioning report to key stakeholders – Disconnect STA Communication Protocols: – DC power system uses CAN and RS485 communication protocols. Follow these steps to properly start up system: 1. After system is evacuated, fully open liquid and vapor service valves. 2. Unit is shipped with valve stem(s) front seated (closed) and caps installed. Replace stem caps after system is opened to refrigerant flow. Replace caps finger-tight and tighten with wrench an additional 1/12 turn. 3. Set room thermostat at desired temperature. Be sure set point is below indoor ambient temperature. 4. Set room thermostat to COOL and fan control to ON or AUTO mode, as desired. Operate unit for 15 minutes. Check system refrigerant charge. Apply Safety Labels Install safety labels in accordance to local code, ensure proper labels are installed. Before installing, modifying, or servicing system, main electrical disconnect switch must be in the OFF position. There may be more than one (1) disconnect switch. Lock out and tag switch with a suitable warning label. Service and Maintenance Safety The DC Power System contains live hazardous voltage and shall only be serviced and maintained by Carrier trained personnel. Read this entire document to understand risks and hazards before servicing this equipment. Prior to service, always shut off or remove the AC disconnect to the HVAC equipment which will disable the electronics in the DC Power System and prevent any system remote control. Always ensure AC power is disconnected before service or maintenance. The AC disconnect on the sub-panel is used to energize the HVAC system and accessory DC Power System. In certain circumstances, Carrier may maintain and/or control the DC Power System and have the ability to start/stop equipment from operating. Periodic Maintenance For continuing high performance and to minimize possible equipment failure, periodic maintenance must be performed on this equipment. Frequency of maintenance may vary depending upon geographic areas, such as coastal applications. See Owner's Manual for information. Battery Handling, Decommissioning, and Disposal For the decommissioning and recycling of the LFP battery pack for Carrier's Battery enabled heat pump, you must contact Carrier Support to initiate the process. Only qualified, trained professionals can handle the complex, potentially hazardous LFP battery pack. The decommissioning process includes system shutdown, disconnection, removal and shipment by Carrier authorized partners, in accordance with DOT guidelines, to specialized recycling facilities, ensuring 100% of materials are recovered and never landfilled. Component Replacement, Service, and Accessories In certain circumstances, the DC Power System may be maintained, monitored, controlled, and/or serviced by Carrier. No maintenance or ongoing inspection of the DC Power System is required by the homeowner. Telemetry from the system will be monitored remotely and any issues observed will be addressed by Carrier. DC Power System Removal, replacement, service and maintenance shall be managed through Carrier and/or its authorized representatives and will only be performed by trained personnel. This equipment has no scheduled maintenance or service needed unless determined by Carrier.
